L2239@P51: Accounting Research and Critical Thinking (D252A) - Companies often rely on accountants to conduct research so they
L2240@P51: can understand economic and financial conditions. This research enables accountants to gather and present information
L2241@P51: to assist leaders in their decision-making processes. In this graduate-level course, students hone research application
L2242@P51: skills by identifying accounting issues and researching concepts related to public accounting firms, businesses, and
L2243@P51: regulating authorities. They develop analytical and critical-thinking capabilities and learn to apply their technical
L2244@P51: knowledge of accounting theory to solve complex accounting problems. This expertise helps them become greater
L2245@P51: assets in the accounting field.

L2283@P52: AI Task Automation (AITA) - This course teaches students to identify repetitive work tasks suited to AI automation. They
L2284@P52: explore which task components are appropriate for it, weighing risk and complexity. Students then design prompts and
L2285@P52: build multi-step AI-automated workflows, connecting AI-generated outputs to complete real tasks. By the end, students
L2286@P52: will be able to incorporate AI automation into their own workflows to streamline everyday work processes.
L2287@P52: American Politics and the U.S. Constitution (C963A) - American Politics and the U.S. Constitution examines the evolution
L2288@P52: of representative government in the United States and the changing interpretations of the civil rights and civil liberties
L2289@P52: protected by the Constitution. This course will give candidates an understanding of the powers of the branches of the
L2290@P52: federal government, the continual tensions inherent in a federal system, the shifting relationship between state and
L2291@P52: federal governments, and the interactions between elected officials and the ever-changing electorate. This course will
L2292@P52: focus on such topics as the role of a free press in a democracy, the impact of changing demographics on American
L2293@P52: politics, and the debates over and expansion of civil rights. Upon completion of the course, candidates should be able to
L2294@P52: explain the basic functions of the federal government, describe the forces that shape American policy and politics, and be
L2295@P52: better prepared to participate in America’s civic institutions.
L2296@P52: Applied Algebra (C957A) - Applied Algebra is designed to help you develop competence in working with functions, the
L2297@P52: algebra of functions, and using some applied properties of functions. You will start learning about how we can apply
L2298@P52-53: © Western Governors University October 27, 2026 53different kinds of functions to relevant, real-life examples. From there, the algebra of several families of functions will be
L2299@P53: explored, including linear, polynomial, exponential, and logistic functions. You will also learn about relevant, applicable
L2300@P53: mathematical properties of each family of functions, including rate of change, concavity, maximizing/minimizing, and
L2301@P53: asymptotes. These properties will be used to solve problems related to your major and make sense of everyday living
L2302@P53: problems.
L2303@P53: Back-End Coding: Java and Job Readiness (CSBE) - The first thing we might notice when visiting a website or
L2304@P53: application is its aesthetic and layout. But as we begin to navigate, we quickly discover that a site’s performance is as
L2305@P53: important as how it looks. The purpose of back-end web development is to ensure that a website or application operates
L2306@P53: efficiently beyond the appealing graphics and design. This is crucial for creating web applications that users can rely on
L2307@P53: and trust. In this offering, students will explore Java programming for beginners. They will also work toward mastering
L2308@P53: algorithms and data structures in Java.
L2309@P53: Basic Skills for Educators (BSE) - Students who aspire to be teachers must attain basic skills in reading, writing, and
L2310@P53: mathematics. In this course, students engage with these subjects and gain knowledge that helps prepare them to
L2311@P53: become effective educators. They explore mathematical concepts, analytical reading, and essay writing. Along the way,
L2312@P53: they encounter the same types of questions, problems, and passages that appear on standard exams required for
L2313@P53: teacher licensure in many states.
L2314@P53: Build Your Strategy (ESHIP2) - This interactive, project-based course gives aspiring entrepreneurs the tools and
L2315@P53: strategies to confidently launch and grow a business. Students define their brand identity by creating a visual brand
L2316@P53: board, writing a compelling brand story, and selecting key marketing channels to reach their target audience. They
L2317@P53: sharpen their financial planning skills and reflect on the challenges of financial decision-making. In addition, students
L2318@P53: explore how to choose the best legal structure for their business by evaluating factors like liability, ownership, taxes, and
L2319@P53: scalability.

L777@P19: School of Technology Admission Requirements
L778@P19: Degree programs from WGU's School of Technology focus on providing the skills, knowledge, certifications, and
L779@P19: credentials students need to be a successful IT pro. Below are admissions requirements specific to School of Technology
L780@P19: programs that are in addition to WGU’s general admissions requirements.

L782@P19-20: © Western Governors University October 27, 2026 20Special Requirements for WGU’s B.S. AI Engineering Program:
L783@P20: Students must demonstrate readiness for advanced mathematics and programming coursework required in the B.S. AI
L784@P20: Engineering program. Students must meet the following admission requirements for admittance to this program:
L785@P20: • Possess a high school diploma or its equivalent.
L786@P20: • Demonstrate readiness through completion of one of the following:
L787@P20: ◦ Option 1: Submit transcripts documenting completion of college-level coursework with a minimum of 2.25
L788@P20: GPA or higher, AND successful and verifiable completion of a precalculus course from a WGU approved
L789@P20: third-party provider with a grade ''C'' or better, AND prior programming coursework equivalent to a score of
L790@P20: 3 or higher on the AP Computer Science A exam (or an approved equivalent programming course).
L791@P20: ◦ Option 2: A high school GPA of 2.75, or higher, AND a B grade, or better, in a high school advanced
L792@P20: mathematics course (precalculus or higher), AND prior programming coursework equivalent to a score of 3
L793@P20: or higher on the AP Computer Science A exam (or an approved equivalent programming course).
L794@P20: Completed college-level coursework in precalculus and computer programming with a grade of B- or better.
L795@P20: Students may complete the Precalculus course and either Introduction to Python Programming OR
L796@P20: Foundations of Coding for a $25 course fee prior to enrolling in the program.
L797@P20: Special Requirements for WGU’s B.S. Computer Science Program:
L798@P20: Students must be able to use key Calculus principles, rules, and applications while in the B.S. Computer Science
L799@P20: program. Students must meet the following admission requirements for admittance to this program:
L800@P20: • Possess a high school diploma or its equivalent.
L801@P20: • Demonstrate readiness through completion of one of the following:
L802@P20: ◦ Option 1: Submit transcripts documenting completion of college-level coursework with a minimum of 2.25
L803@P20: GPA or higher, AND successful and verifiable completion of a precalculus course from a WGU approved
L804@P20: third-party provider with a grade ''C'' or better.
L805@P20: ◦ Option 2: A high school GPA of 2.75, AND successful, verifiable completion of a precalculus (or higher
L806@P20: level) advanced mathematics course with a grade of B or better.
L807@P20: If no previous PreCalculus course has been completed by the time of application, students can complete this course prior
L808@P20: to matriculation.
L809@P20: Special Requirements for all other WGU IT bachelor's degree programs:
L810@P20: To be considered for enrollment into these programs, students must possess a high school diploma or its equivalent and
L811@P20: demonstrate program readiness through one of the following:
L812@P20: • Option 1: Submit transcripts documenting completion of college-level coursework with a minimum of 2.25 GPA or
L813@P20: higher.
L814@P20: • Option 2: Possess a bachelors or associate degree (A.A, A.S. or A.A.S. acceptable) from an accredited postsecondary institution.
L815@P20: • Option 3: Submit official record of completion of a transferable IT certification, some of which may provide transfer
L816@P20: credit into various programs.
L817@P20: • Option 4: Submit high school transcripts with a minimum GPA of 2.75.
L818@P20: • Option 5: Submit transcripts documenting completion of previous IT coursework (must be 300 level or higher).

L820@P20: • Possess a bachelor’s degree in a STEM field, Business degree (Quantitative Analysis, Accounting, Economics,
L821@P20: Finance, or degree with similar quantitative focus). OR
L822@P20: • Possess any bachelor’s degree PLUS one of the following:
L823@P20: ◦ Relevant and current IT certification
L824@P20: ◦ Related IT coursework
L825@P20: Special Requirements for WGU’s M.S. Information Technology Program:
L826@P20: • Possess a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
L827@P20-21: © Western Governors University October 27, 2026 21Special Requirements for WGU’s M.S. Data Analytics Program:

L829@P21: • Possess any bachelor’s degree PLUS one of the following:

L840@P21: course within a given period and matriculate, the $99 investment will go toward their tuition with WGU.

L842@P21: Programmer, PCAD™–Certified Associate Data Analyst with Python, or IBM Data Science Professional
L843@P21: Certificate.

L845@P21: To be considered for enrollment into this program, students must possess any bachelor’s degree from an accredited
L846@P21: institution plus ONE of the following:
L847@P21: • Option 1: Students with a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science may enroll directly into one of the
L848@P21: three enrollable graduate code programs.
L849@P21: • Option 2: Students with a bachelor's degree in a field other than Computer Science must complete the
L850@P21: Foundations of Computer Science course prior to enrolling in the program.
